arm_c_atomic_full_budget.prompt_note: Generated under the original wording ('use most of that budget'). The profile has since been retargeted to ~900 words with a hard 1,024 ceiling; these numbers predate that change.

arm_d_focused_citations.change: Removed the 'cite every reference' instruction; told the model to cite the single best supporting document and add more only if each independently supports the object.
arm_d_focused_citations.pipeline_change: Added trim_to_word_limit and normalize_generated_record, so the word cap and the all-cited rule are enforced deterministically instead of by prompt.

caveats: Four topics; consistent direction but not a significance test.
Generation is high variance: the same default config produced 9 and then 28 answer objects for topic 58 in different runs.
Judge changed from gpt-5.5 to DeepSeek V4 Flash, so absolute values are not comparable across records; the A/B contrast within this record is consistent.
Automated assignment scores above NIST manual assignment.

citation_count_effect.description: Full Support rate collapses as citations per object rise; measured on arm C.
citation_count_effect.mechanism: The all-cited rule forced long reference lists to be covered by padding two or three citations onto nearly every object; trailing citations frequently do not support the claim.

design: Four development topics generated under both prompt profiles. Retrieval, generator model and judge held fixed. Judge is DeepSeek V4 Flash for every cell.

four_arm_summary.caveat: Four topics. Generation variance alone has produced 9 versus 28 objects for the same config, so coverage differences of this size are not resolved.
four_arm_summary.recommendation: Arm D. It wins every citation-support metric both as generated and at the oracle repair ceiling, and because every object carries exactly one citation its wp_all equals wp_first by construction, so it cannot be diluted on the all-judged variant. It gives up 0.047 strict_vital against arm A for +0.217 weighted precision and +0.410 hard precision.

generation_reliability.implication: About one topic in four fails first time. Over 119 topics that is ~30 resumes at $0.71 each.
generation_reliability.note: Uncited-reference failures are self-imposed; the guidelines state uncited references do not hurt the score.

generation_reliability_arm_d.note: Normalization eliminated the uncited-reference mode entirely. The word cap became the dominant failure, which is why a deterministic trim was added.

length.note: Neither arm approaches the cap. Nugget scoring is pure recall with no length penalty.

supersedes: The two-topic comparison in dev_ragdoll_nugget_eval_spike_v1, which reported atomic as neutral-to-better on coverage.

three_arm_summary.reading: No arm dominates. B has by far the cleanest citations (11% No Support against 30% for both A and C) and the best weighted precision. C recovers most of B's coverage loss and posts the best strict_all and hard_precision, but its citation error rate returns to A's level: pushing length appears to make the model assert more than it can ground.
